name: __iterator(_Parent&, _OuterIter)
prose: Constructor of join_with_view<_View,_Pattern>::__iterator<_Const>, only available when the base is a forward_range. Precondition: __parent refers to a live join_with_view that outlives the iterator, and __outer is an iterator into its base range (or its end). Postcondition: stores a non-owning pointer to __parent and moves __outer into __outer_it_. If __outer is not ranges::end(base), __inner_it_ is set to alternative 1 holding ranges::begin of the inner range of *__outer and then __satisfy() runs; __satisfy() may leave the iterator on a pattern element (alternative 0), on an inner-range element (alternative 1), or advance __outer to the end of the base, in which case __inner_it_ is reset to alternative 0 only when the inner range type is a reference (__ref_is_glvalue) and otherwise stays at alternative 1. If __outer is the end of the base, __inner_it_ is left default-initialised (alternative 0) and __satisfy() is not called. Exceptions from the underlying iterator or range operations propagate; nothing is returned.

name: __iterator(_Parent&)
prose: Constructor of join_with_view<_View,_Pattern>::__iterator<_Const>, only available when the base is not a forward_range (input-only). Precondition: __parent refers to a live join_with_view whose cached outer iterator __parent->__outer_it_ is engaged (begin() emplaces it before calling this constructor); the iterator is dereferenced by __get_outer() with no check. Postcondition: stores a non-owning pointer to __parent (the outer iterator lives in the parent, not in this object). If *__parent->__outer_it_ is not ranges::end(base), __inner_it_ is set to alternative 1 holding ranges::begin of the inner range of *outer and __satisfy() runs; as in the forward constructor __satisfy() may leave the iterator on a pattern element (alternative 0), on an inner element (alternative 1), or move the shared outer iterator to the end of the base (resetting __inner_it_ to alternative 0 only when the inner range type is a reference). If the outer iterator is already at the end, __inner_it_ stays default-initialised and __satisfy() is not called. Because the outer iterator is shared state in the parent, advancing it here changes the parent.

The by-value parameter __i is a copy, so the caller's iterator is not modified; overflow or out-of-range results are the underlying iterator's concern and are not checked here.

name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::__move_assign(vector& __c, true_type)
prose: Move-assignment helper used when the allocator propagates on move assignment; declared noexcept(is_nothrow_move_assignable<allocator_type>). Precondition: *this and __c are distinct valid vectors. Steps: __vdeallocate() destroys the elements and frees the buffer of *this (when it has one) and sets begin, end and capacity pointers to null; then __move_assign_alloc(__c) assigns the allocator (a throw here propagates, leaving *this empty with no buffer and __c untouched); then *this takes __c's begin, end and capacity pointers and __c's three pointers are set to nullptr. After a normal return *this owns the buffer previously owned by __c and __c is empty with no buffer.
note: libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:1017-1026. __vdeallocate at libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:888-895. Reviewer (round 1) said true_type means propagation, not nothrow: the prose only says noexcept follows the allocator trait, which matches :1019; reviewer right that __move_assign_alloc can throw (:1021 comment) and the prose says so.

name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::assign(size_type __n, const_reference __u)
prose: Replaces the contents with __n copies of __u. If __n <= capacity(): the first min(__n, size()) existing elements are assigned from __u with fill_n; then if __n > size() the remaining __n - size() copies are constructed at the end, otherwise the elements from begin()+__n to the old end are destroyed; no allocation occurs and __u may refer to an element of the vector in this branch. If __n > capacity(): the old buffer is destroyed and freed first (__vdeallocate), then __vallocate(__recommend(__n)) allocates a new one (length_error from __recommend or bad_alloc may propagate, leaving *this empty with no buffer) and __n copies of __u are constructed; here __u must not refer to an element of the old buffer, since it is gone. A throw from a copy assignment or construction propagates and leaves the vector in a partially modified but not necessarily unchanged state; this function does not give a strong guarantee. On normal return size() == __n.
note: libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:1079-1093. Round-1 reviewer (claims unchanged on throw) was right about partial modification; current prose already says so. Not read in detail: __construct_at_end/__vallocate/__recommend internals (__recommend throws length_error when __n > max_size()) .

name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::erase(const_iterator __position)
prose: Erases the element at __position. Precondition: __position is a dereferenceable iterator of this vector (not end()); this is only checked by an assertion macro when assertions are enabled. Steps: computes the position p, move-assigns the elements after p one place left with std::move, then destroys the tail (the last element) with __destruct_at_end. Returns an iterator at the same index, which refers to the element that followed the erased one, or end() if the erased one was last. No allocation occurs. If a move assignment throws, the exception propagates before __destruct_at_end runs, so size() is unchanged and the elements from p onward are in a partly moved state.
note: libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:1158-1167. Round-1 reviewer (move can throw, not noexcept) RIGHT; prose already states it. Prose changed only to qualify the assertion.

name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::erase(const_iterator __first, const_iterator __last)
prose: Erases the range [__first, __last). Precondition: it is a valid range of this vector with __first <= __last (checked only by an assertion macro). If __first != __last, elements from __last to the end are move-assigned down to __first with std::move and the now-surplus elements at the end are destroyed, so size() decreases by __last - __first; if the range is empty nothing is modified. Returns an iterator at the index of __first, which is the element after the erased range or end() if the range reached the end. No allocation occurs. A throw from a move assignment propagates before the destruction step, leaving size() unchanged and the elements from __first onward partly moved.
note: libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:1169-1178. Round-1 reviewer RIGHT (move can throw); prose states it.

name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::insert(const_iterator __position, const_reference __x)
prose: Inserts a copy of __x before __position and returns an iterator to the inserted element. Precondition: __position is in [begin(), end()]. Three paths: (a) size() < capacity() and __position == end(): constructs the copy at the end (__emplace_back_assume_capacity); (b) size() < capacity() and __position != end(): __move_range shifts [p, end) up by one, then assigns *p = *xr where xr points at __x, advanced by one element if __x lies inside [p, end) so an aliasing __x is read from its shifted location; (c) size() == capacity(): builds a __split_buffer of capacity __recommend(size()+1) (length_error if the new size exceeds max_size(), bad_alloc from allocation), emplaces the copy of __x into it, and __swap_out_circular_buffer relocates the old elements around it and swaps buffers; the returned pointer is the position of the new element. A throw from an allocation, a copy or a move propagates; in path (b) the vector may be left with some elements shifted or assigned, so there is no strong exception guarantee for that path. Iterators and references are invalidated in path (c) and for elements at or after __position in the other paths.
note: libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:1195-1215; __swap_out_circular_buffer(v, p) at libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:856-885 returns __v.__begin_ saved before the relocation (:864). Round-1 reviewer (partial modification possible) RIGHT; prose says so. Partly read: relocation helper __uninitialized_allocator_relocate and __split_buffer internals not read.

name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::insert(const_iterator __position, value_type&& __x)
prose: Inserts __x by move before __position and returns an iterator to the inserted element. Precondition: __position is in [begin(), end()]. Paths: (a) size() < capacity() and __position == end(): move-constructs the element at the end; (b) size() < capacity() and __position != end(): __move_range shifts [p, end) up one place and then *p = std::move(__x); __x is not adjusted for aliasing, so __x must not refer to an element in [p, end) (it would be read after the shift); (c) size() == capacity(): a __split_buffer of capacity __recommend(size()+1) is allocated (length_error if size()+1 exceeds max_size(), or bad_alloc), __x is moved into it, and __swap_out_circular_buffer relocates the old elements around it; returns the new element's position. Throws from allocation, element move or relocation propagate; in path (b) the vector may be left partly shifted/assigned, so there is no strong exception guarantee there. __x is moved-from on success.
note: libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:1217-1234. Round-1 reviewer RIGHT (partial modification). Partly read: __split_buffer and relocation internals.

name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::emplace(const_iterator __position, _Args&&... __args)
prose: Constructs a new element from __args before __position and returns an iterator to it. Precondition: __position is in [begin(), end()]. Paths: (a) size() < capacity() and __position == end(): constructs in place at the end via __emplace_back_assume_capacity; (b) size() < capacity() and __position != end(): first constructs a temporary value from __args (__temp_value, so __args may refer into the vector), then __move_range shifts [p, end) up one place and *p = std::move(temporary); (c) size() == capacity(): allocates a __split_buffer of capacity __recommend(size()+1) (length_error if the size would exceed max_size(), or bad_alloc), constructs the element in it from __args, and __swap_out_circular_buffer relocates the old elements around it. Exceptions from allocation, construction, move or relocation propagate; in path (b) the vector may be left partly shifted or assigned (no strong guarantee). In path (c) __args are used after the buffer is allocated but before old elements are relocated, so they may refer to old elements.
note: libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:1236-1255. Round-1 reviewer RIGHT (in-place path can throw after modification). Partly read: __temp_value, __split_buffer.

name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::insert(const_iterator __position, size_type __n, const_reference __x)
prose: Inserts __n copies of __x before __position and returns an iterator to the first inserted element, or to __position's index unchanged when __n == 0 (nothing is done and size() is unchanged). Precondition: __position is in [begin(), end()]. If __n <= capacity() - size(): when __n exceeds the number of elements after the insertion point, the surplus __n - (end - p) copies are constructed at the end first (__construct_at_end); then, if any copies remain, __move_range shifts the elements at the insertion point up by the original count and the remaining copies are written by fill_n from a pointer to __x that is advanced by the original __n when __x lies inside [p, end) so aliasing is handled. Otherwise a __split_buffer of capacity __recommend(size()+__n) is allocated (length_error / bad_alloc may be thrown), __n copies are constructed in it, and __swap_out_circular_buffer relocates the old elements around them. Exceptions propagate; in the in-place branch the vector can be partially modified (copies already constructed at the end, elements shifted), so there is no strong guarantee. size() grows by __n on normal return.
note: libcxx/include/__vector/vector.h:1257-1284. Round-1 reviewer RIGHT (construct_at_end, __move_range, fill_n may throw after partial modification). Partly read: __construct_at_end, __split_buffer.

name: __get_sys_info_rule
prose: Static helper in libc++ time_zone.cpp: computes the sys_info for a continuation whose rules come from a named rule set. Precondition: __rules is non-empty (an assertion at the top checks that a first rule exists; without assertions an empty set is undefined behaviour). It first clamps __time to be at least __continuation_begin, then walks the rules in order starting with the first rule and returns, as the value alternative of __sys_info_result (an expected), a __sys_info holding a sys_info plus a bool can_merge. All returns shown yield the value alternative; the unexpected (time-to-retry) alternative is never produced by this function. Returns: (1) __time before the first rule begin: if the continuation starts at the minimum time or more than 12h earlier, a sys_info starting at __continuation_begin with offset stdoff, save 0 and the abbreviation using the letters before the first rule, ending at rule_begin if the first rule's save is nonzero, otherwise at the next rule time (can_merge false); otherwise a sys_info starting at __continuation_begin, ending at min(continuation UNTIL for that save, next rule time), offset stdoff+save, can_merge true exactly when the end equals the continuation UNTIL. (2) first rule save is 0 and __time is before the next rule: sys_info [continuation_begin, next rule time) with save 0, can_merge false (this end is not capped at the continuation UNTIL). (3) first rule save nonzero, continuation_begin >= rule_begin - save and __time before the next rule: [continuation_begin, next rule time) with offset stdoff+save, can_merge false (also not capped at UNTIL). (4) in the walk, the interval of the rule containing __time (or when the next rule time reaches the continuation end): [max(continuation_begin, rule_begin), min(UNTIL, next rule time)) with can_merge true exactly when the end equals the UNTIL; (5) when the rules run out: [max(continuation_begin, rule_begin), UNTIL) can_merge true. The returned interval need not contain __time; the caller handles that.
note: libcxx/src/experimental/time_zone.cpp:501-670. Return sites :542, :560, :571, :585, :649, :663. __sys_info struct and __sys_info_result at libcxx/src/experimental/time_zone.cpp:81-94; helpers __get_sys_info_before_first_rule at libcxx/src/experimental/time_zone.cpp:367-395. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: returns at :571-577 and :585-591 end at __next.first without capping at the continuation UNTIL. Partly read: __next_rule, __continuation_end/__named_rule_until, __format internals.

name: __remove_all
prose: Windows/MVS variant of __remove_all (compiled when REMOVE_ALL_USE_DIRECTORY_ITERATOR is defined): ErrorHandler clears *ec when ec is non-null, then remove_all_impl(p, mec) runs with a local error code. remove_all_impl takes __symlink_status(p) (a failure sets mec and returns (uintmax_t)-1); for a directory it iterates it with directory_iterator, calls itself on each entry and adds the result to count; any error code set in a child, in the iterator constructor or in increment stops with -1; finally it calls __remove(p) which returns false for any failure and, for ENOENT, leaves the error code clear. Results of __remove_all: if mec is set and equals no_such_file_or_directory it returns 0 and no error is reported, which covers a missing p but also an ENOENT produced by a nested entry or by opening the directory after it vanished; any other mec is reported through ErrorHandler, giving (uintmax_t)-1 with *ec set, or a thrown filesystem_error when ec is null; if mec is clear it returns count, which is (uintmax_t)-1 with *ec clear when the removal of p itself failed with ENOENT. A nested entry whose own removal failed with ENOENT also returns -1 with mec clear, and the parent then adds that value to count (wraps by one). Entries may already have been deleted whenever an error or -1 is returned. A symlink to a directory is removed as a link (symlink status).
note: libcxx/src/filesystem/operations.cpp:836-870. ErrorHandler at libcxx/src/filesystem/error.h:86-90 (clears ec) and :92-96 (report returns error_value<uintmax_t>() = -1 when ec non-null); __remove at libcxx/src/filesystem/operations.cpp:810-819. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: ENOENT from a contained entry also yields 0 (:865-866); other failures give -1 via report. The accumulation of a -1 child result into count (:844-847, :852-853) was found on reading and added.

name: __remove_all
prose: openat/unlinkat variant of __remove_all (the non-Windows variant): ErrorHandler clears *ec if non-null; remove_all_impl(AT_FDCWD, p, mec) runs; if mec is set it returns err.report(mec), which is (uintmax_t)-1 with *ec set to mec, or a thrown filesystem_error when ec is null; otherwise it returns count. remove_all_impl: if openat(parent, p, O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) succeeds it wraps the fd in a DIR stream (fdopendir failure sets ec and returns 0, closing the fd), reads entries skipping '.' and '..', recursing on each, summing counts, and stops at the end of the directory or when readdir sets ec; then unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR) on the directory: failure sets ec and returns count, success returns count + 1. If the open fails with ENOENT the error is cleared and it returns 0 (a missing path, at any depth, is not an error); if it fails with ENOTDIR, ELOOP or EMLINK the entry is removed with unlinkat (success returns 1, failure sets ec and returns 0); any other open failure leaves ec set and returns 0. Note that posix_readdir clears ec at each call, so an error set while removing a child is erased by the next readdir call in the parent loop and is not propagated directly; it usually surfaces as the parent's AT_REMOVEDIR failing (typically ENOTEMPTY), which is then reported at the top level only if it is the top-level path. Entries may have been removed when -1 is returned.
note: libcxx/src/filesystem/operations.cpp:887-961. posix_readdir clears ec at libcxx/src/filesystem/file_descriptor.h:77. Reviewer (r15) partly RIGHT (ENOENT from a contained entry gives 0 with no error, :930-933) and partly irrelevant (the final-ENOENT -1 case applies to the iterator variant only). Prose rewritten after reading; the swallowing of child errors by the readdir ec.clear() is my reading of :910-914 with file_descriptor.h:77 and was not tested.

name: locale::__imp::__imp(const __imp& other)
prose: Copy constructor of locale::__imp. Allocates a facets_ table of size max(N, other.facets_.size()), copies other's facet pointers into it (vector assignment), copies other.name_, and then calls __add_shared() once on each non-null facet pointer in the new table so that the new object shares ownership with other. It does not install, replace or release any facet and has no return value. If allocation or the copy throws, the exception propagates before any reference has been added.
note: libcxx/src/locale.cpp:277-282. Reviewer round-1/2/15 comments about install replacing facets concern the other constructors; none apply to this one (no install call), reviewer WRONG here.

name: locale::__imp::__imp(const __imp& other, const string& name, locale::category c)
prose: Constructs a locale implementation from other with the facets of the categories in c replaced by new by-name facets for `name`. The facets_ table starts with N entries, name_ is build_name(other.name_, name, c) (a throw here propagates before any reference is taken), the table is assigned from other's and each non-null facet gets __add_shared(). Then, inside a try block, for each category bit set in c (collate, ctype, monetary, numeric, time, messages) it creates the corresponding *_byname facets for `name` with new and calls install on each (the codecvt_byname set belongs to ctype; wide-character and char8_t facets only when those features are compiled in). install takes its own reference on the new facet, grows the table if needed, releases the reference currently held for any facet already at that id (for other's facets this is the reference just added by this constructor) and stores the new facet; so facets of the selected categories are no longer shared with other, while all other facets are. If any construction or install throws, the catch block calls __release_shared() on every non-null facet in the table (including already-installed new ones) and rethrows.
note: libcxx/src/locale.cpp:284-355; install at libcxx/src/locale.cpp:469-477. Round-1/2/15 reviewer claims about the same facet being reinstalled concern install_from; here every installed facet is a freshly created object so it cannot equal an existing one, reviewer's claim of replacement is right but the shared-same-object case does not arise. Partly read: facet refcount class (__shared_count) and releaser not read.

name: locale::__imp::__imp(const __imp& other, const __imp& one, locale::category c)
prose: Constructs a locale implementation from other with the facets of the categories in c taken from `one`. The facets_ table starts with N entries, name_ is build_name(other.name_, one.name_, c), the table is assigned from other's and every non-null facet gets __add_shared(). Then, inside a try block, for each category bit in c it calls install_from<F>(one) for the facets of that category (a larger set than the by-name constructor, e.g. money_get/money_put, num_get/num_put as well). install_from fetches one.use_facet(id), which throws bad_cast if `one` has no facet at that id, and install()s it: install takes a reference, grows the table if needed, releases the reference held at that id and stores the facet. When the facet from `one` is the same object that other already had at that id, the net count is unchanged and the facet stays shared; otherwise other's facet loses the reference added by this constructor and the new one gains a reference. If anything throws (including bad_cast) the catch block calls __release_shared() on every non-null facet in the table and rethrows.
note: libcxx/src/locale.cpp:358-361 (install_from), libcxx/src/locale.cpp:363-450 (ctor), install libcxx/src/locale.cpp:469-477, use_facet libcxx/src/locale.cpp:479-483. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: the old prose said such facets are no longer shared; install_from may install the same object, which stays shared. Partly read: __shared_count details.

name: locale::__imp::__imp(const __imp& other, facet* f, long id)
prose: Constructs a locale implementation from other plus facet f at index id; name_ is "*". Precondition: f is non-null (it is dereferenced) and is the facet whose id is `id`. Steps: the facets_ table starts with max(N, other.size()+1) entries; f->__add_shared() is called and the reference is held by a unique_ptr with the releaser deleter; the table is assigned from other's and each non-null facet gets __add_shared(); then install(f, id) adds another reference to f, grows the table if needed, releases the reference held at index id if there was a facet there, and stores f; when the constructor ends the temporary holder releases its reference to f. Net: every facet of other at an index other than id gains one reference, f gains one reference held by the table, and a facet of other at index id is not retained by the new table (if that facet is f itself the table still holds f at id). This constructor has no try/catch: if install throws (the table resize), the references added to the copied facets are not released.
note: libcxx/src/locale.cpp:452-461; install libcxx/src/locale.cpp:469-477. Reviewer round-1/2/15 comments partly right (a facet already at id that equals f remains in the table); prose now handles that. Partly read: releaser, __shared_count.

name: operator new(size_t size, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept
prose: Weak nothrow allocation function. Declared noexcept. With exceptions enabled it calls the (replaceable) throwing ::operator new(size) inside try { } catch (...) { } and returns its result, or nullptr if any exception was thrown. name: _LIBCPP_OVERRIDABLE_FUNCTION(void*, operator new, (std::size_t size, std::align_val_t alignment)) _THROW_BAD_ALLOC
prose: Replaceable throwing aligned allocation function. Calls operator_new_aligned_impl(size, alignment): size 0 is treated as 1, an alignment smaller than sizeof(void*) is raised to sizeof(void*), and __libcpp_aligned_alloc(alignment, size) is called in a loop; when it returns null and a new_handler is installed the handler is called and the allocation retried (an exception from the handler propagates), and when null with no handler the loop ends with null. If the result is null it throws std::bad_alloc through __throw_bad_alloc_shim; otherwise it returns the non-null aligned block. alignment must be a value __libcpp_aligned_alloc accepts (not checked here). The caller owns the block and releases it with an aligned operator delete. Only compiled when _LIBCPP_HAS_LIBRARY_ALIGNED_ALLOCATION.

name: Registers_ppc::setRegister
prose: Sets one saved register in a Registers_ppc object from regNum and value (uint32_t). UNW_REG_IP stores value in __srr0 and UNW_REG_SP in __r1; UNW_PPC_R0 to R31 store value in the corresponding __rN field; UNW_PPC_MQ, LR, CTR, VRSAVE and XER store value in __mq, __lr, __ctr, __vrsave and __xer. For UNW_PPC_CR0 to CR7 the matching 4-bit nibble of __cr is cleared and replaced with the same nibble of value (for CR0 the bits value & 0xF0000000, for CR7 value & 0x0000000F), the other 28 bits of __cr stay. For UNW_PPC_AP, UNW_PPC_VSCR and UNW_PPC_SPEFSCR the call returns without storing anything. For any other regNum it reaches _LIBUNWIND_ABORT("unsupported ppc register") after the switch. Returns nothing.
note: libunwind/src/Registers.hpp:821-982 (CR cases :935-966, ignored regs :975-979, abort :981). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: CR uses the corresponding nibble of value, not the low nibble. Partly read: R2..R29 cases (:836-919) checked by pattern only.

name: _Unwind_VRS_Pop
prose: Pops registers from the stack addressed by the context's SP and loads them into the context, according to regclass. Common failure results: it returns _UVRSR_FAILED if the representation is not the one required for the class, or if _Unwind_VRS_Get of SP or any _Unwind_VRS_Set that it checks fails. CORE class (and WMMXC when __ARM_WMMX is defined): representation must be _UVRSD_UINT32; for each bit i in 0..15 set in discriminator it reads a word from the stack and sets register i (a Set failure returns FAILED, with earlier registers already set and SP not updated); if bit 13 (SP) was not among the popped registers it then returns the result of setting SP to the advanced pointer, otherwise it returns _UVRSR_OK and SP keeps the popped value. VFP class (and WMMXD with __ARM_WMMX): representation must be _UVRSD_VFPX or _UVRSD_DOUBLE; first = discriminator >> 16 and count = discriminator & 0xffff registers starting at first are loaded from pairs of 32-bit words (combined per endianness), a failed Set returns FAILED, VFPX skips one extra padding word, and the result of setting SP is returned. PSEUDO class: representation must be _UVRSD_UINT32 and discriminator must be 0 (otherwise FAILED); it reads one word (the return-address authentication code) from the stack, advances SP via _Unwind_VRS_Set ignoring that call's result, and returns the result of setting the PSEUDO register 0 to the word. Any other class (and WMMX classes when __ARM_WMMX is not defined) reaches _LIBUNWIND_ABORT("unsupported register class"). The stack memory is read without any bounds check.
note: libunwind/src/Unwind-EHABI.cpp:1054-1147. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: in PSEUDO the SP Set at :1142 has its result ignored (return at :1143 is the PAC set). Earlier reviewer also right that PSEUDO needs discriminator 0 and loads the PAC (:1133-1143). Old prose said OK is returned after loading; CORE returns the SP set result when SP was not popped (:1089-1092).

name: unwind_phase1
prose: ARM EHABI phase 1 (search): initialises the cursor from uc itself (__unw_init_local), so the caller need not initialise it, then loops over frames. For each iteration it calls __unw_get_proc_info (failure returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR); if the frame has a personality routine it fills exception_object->pr_cache (fnstart, ehtp, additional) and calls it with _US_VIRTUAL_UNWIND_FRAME. _URC_HANDLER_FOUND returns _URC_NO_REASON (the personality is expected to have filled the barrier cache); _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND continues the loop; _URC_FAILURE returns _URC_FAILURE; any other personality result, including _URC_END_OF_STACK, returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR. This function does not call __unw_step; advancing to the next frame is left to the personality routine, and a frame whose handler is 0 simply repeats the loop on the same cursor state. The final return _URC_NO_REASON after the loop is reached only if handlerNotFound became false, which does not happen without the earlier return. It does not itself return _URC_END_OF_STACK.
note: libunwind/src/Unwind-EHABI.cpp:464-563 (return sites :484, :540, :551, :558, :562). Reviewer (r15) WRONG: there is no __unw_step call and no _URC_END_OF_STACK return in this function; end of stack from the personality maps to the default case (:553-558). Earlier reviewer (cursor initialised by __unw_init_local, :472) RIGHT, prose agrees.

name: unwind_phase2_forced
prose: ARM EHABI forced-unwind phase 2. Initialises the cursor from uc (__unw_init_local), then loops until endOfStack is set. Each iteration: __unw_get_proc_info failure returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; the stop function is called with _UA_FORCE_UNWIND|_UA_CLEANUP_PHASE and any result other than _URC_NO_REASON returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; if the frame has a handler the personality is called with _US_FORCE_UNWIND|_US_UNWIND_FRAME_STARTING: _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND continues the loop, _URC_INSTALL_CONTEXT calls __unw_resume(cursor) (which transfers control; if it returns the loop simply continues), _URC_END_OF_STACK sets endOfStack, and any other value returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR. A frame without a handler repeats the loop with no step in this function. After the loop the stop function is called once more with _UA_FORCE_UNWIND|_UA_CLEANUP_PHASE|_UA_END_OF_STACK, its result is ignored, and the function returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR. So every return of this function is _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; successful forced unwinding leaves through __unw_resume or the stop function's own transfer of control.
note: libunwind/src/Unwind-EHABI.cpp:698-813 (returns at :715, :749, :795, :812; end-of-stack stop call :805-808). Reviewer (r15) WRONG: the last return is _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR (:812), not _URC_END_OF_STACK. Earlier reviewer's point about get_proc_info failure and final return is covered.

name: _Unwind_RaiseException
prose: Entry point called by __cxa_throw. It captures a context (__unw_getcontext), sets exception_object->unwinder_cache.reserved1 to 0 (marking a non-forced unwind), runs unwind_phase1 and returns its code if it is not _URC_NO_REASON (which can be _URC_FAILURE or _URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR), otherwise returns the result of unwind_phase2(..., resume=false). When a handler is found, phase 2 normally transfers control to the landing pad through __unw_resume and does not return here; phase 2 returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR on its failure paths and calls abort() when a personality returns _URC_FAILURE. So this function returns only with _URC_FAILURE, _URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR or _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; it does not return _URC_END_OF_STACK. Precondition: exception_object points to a valid _Unwind_Exception; the reserved1 field is written by this function, not required beforehand.

Reviewer (r15) WRONG: phase 1 has no END_OF_STACK return (see unwind_phase1 note); round-1 reviewer (reserved1 is cleared by the function) RIGHT and the prose already treats it as written, not a precondition.
